editorial.headline: Steel Frames Within the Building Work
editorial.standfirst: A specialist construction activity open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Steel-frame installation is a specialist activity within building construction: the work of installing steel frameworks as part of a building project. The classification is deliberately narrow. It concerns the assembly of the structural steel frame itself, rather than treating every part of a construction project as one undifferentiated activity. It also carries the Steel Frame Installation sub-classification, KK016.

The activity is open to businesses at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, it is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record presents no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity.

Bali’s position is equally important, and more specific. This activity is not blocked by the province’s PMA moratorium. The stated reason is its OSS risk position at the Besar scale: Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s standing for the activity is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, rather than as a moratorium block.

That distinction matters because Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. Steel-frame installation is not presented in that blocked category. For a foreign-owned business considering this precise construction work in Bali, the record’s conclusion is straightforward: it remains available for PMA registration, with the national ceiling recorded at 100%.
